abstract.text: Can any secrets still be shed by that much studied, uniquely integrable, Elliptic Billiard? Starting by examining the family of 3-periodic trajectories and the loci of their Triangular Centers, one obtains a beautiful and variegated gallery of curves: ellipses, quartics, sextics, circles, and even a stationary point. Secondly, one notices this family conserves an intriguing ratio: Inradius-to-Circumradius. In turn this implies three conservation corollaries: (i) the sum of bounce angle cosines, (ii) the product of excentral cosines, and (iii) the ratio of excentral-to-orbit areas. Monge’s Orthoptic Circle’s close relation to 4-periodic Billiard trajectories is well-known. Its geometry provided clues with which to generalize 3-periodic invariants to trajectories of an arbitrary number of edges. This was quite unexpected. Indeed, the Elliptic Billiard did surprise us!

sections.summary: Introduces the elliptic billiard and asks whether it can still surprise. Reviews prior elliptic-locus results for Incenter, Barycenter, Circumcenter, Orthocenter, and X5; describes the applet/locus gallery; previews the r/R conservation and the Monge Orthoptic Circle bridge to general N.
sections.title: Introduction and Experimental Route to EB Surprises

source_span.end_text: start page 4, through page 5: Hamiltonian integrability, Joachimsthal integral, caustic, Poncelet porism, Monge Orthoptic Circle and N=4 orbit connection.

sections.summary: Sets up the elliptic billiard as an integrable Hamiltonian system with energy and Joachimsthal integrals, discusses the confocal caustic and constant perimeter, and presents Poncelet’s porism and Monge’s Orthoptic Circle as geometric background for N-periodic orbits.
sections.title: Integrability, Conservation, Poncelet, and Monge Geometry

source_span.end_text: start page 6, through page 7: Incenter locus recap, elliptic loci of X1–X5, numerical count of elliptic Kimberling centers.

sections.summary: Recaps the Incenter locus for N=3, states that major centers X1–X4 and X5 have elliptic loci, and reports the numerical finding that only 29 of the first 100 Kimberling centers produce elliptic loci.
sections.title: Triangular Orbit Loci: Incenter and Major Centers

source_span.end_text: start page 7, through page 9: excenter ellipse, derived triangles, extouch triangle, Feuerbach Point and anticomplement behaviors, additional notable loci.

sections.summary: Covers excenter loci, the exceptional status of the Excentral Triangle among derived triangles, the Extouch Triangle as identical to the caustic, and the Feuerbach Point/anticomplement sweeping the caustic and billiard.
sections.title: Excenters, Derived Triangles, and Feuerbach Loci

source_span.end_text: start page 9, through page 10: Mittenpunkt X9 stationarity, affine proof, Circumbilliard corollary.

sections.summary: Presents the surprising stationarity of the Mittenpunkt X9 at the billiard center, sketches the affine proof, and derives the Circumbilliard corollary for every triangle.
sections.title: Stationary Mittenpunkt and Circumbilliard

source_span.end_text: start page 10, through page 13: constant r/R, sum of cosines, product of excentral cosines, excentral-to-orbit area ratio.

sections.summary: Introduces the conserved Inradius-to-Circumradius ratio for the 3-periodic family and derives three conservation corollaries: sum of internal-angle cosines, product of excentral cosines, and excentral-to-orbit area ratio.
sections.title: Constant r/R and Conservation Corollaries

source_span.end_text: page 13 only: circular locus of Q1/Q2, radius formula, Tucker/Cosine Circle interpretation.

sections.summary: Describes a circular locus from intersections of tangent/reflected excentral edges, gives the radius formula in terms of r, L, γ, and identifies the circle as the Cosine Circle of the Excentral Triangle.
sections.title: N=3 Circular Locus

source_span.end_text: start page 14, through page 15: generalized tangential polygon, stationary point, generalized extouchpoints, cosine sum and product for all N.

sections.summary: Generalizes N=3 invariants to N>3 using the tangential polygon: stationary concurrence point, extouchpoint-like caustic sweep, cosine-sum conservation for all N, and conserved tangential cosine product.
sections.title: Generalizing Invariants Beyond N=3

source_span.end_text: page 16 only: odd-N area ratio, arbitrary-N circular loci and proof via momentum conservation.

sections.summary: Shows area-ratio conservation only for odd N, then unifies N=3 and N=4 circular loci by proving that an appropriate intersection locus is a circle of radius 1/γ for arbitrary N.
sections.title: Area Ratios and Circular Loci for N>3

source_span.end_text: page 17 only: conclusion, open questions, list-of-videos setup.

sections.summary: Collects open questions about elliptic versus complicated loci, algebraic status, 3D counterparts, self-intersecting orbits, Poncelet families, spherical/ellipsoidal billiards, and expression of further invariants in γ, L, N.
sections.title: Conclusion and Open Questions
